FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` breaks interface correctness with the advertised sandbox model when tests are supplied. In `bench/endocrine.py`, the patched file is written into a temp directory under its basename only, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. Any test command that references the original source path or project-relative package layout will run against the real repo tree or fail to import the patched module, so the “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature does not actually test the patched code end-to-end. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no project tree copy is created; `test_cmd` is not rewritten; tests are run via `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)`.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluations can be labeled SAFE/NEUTRAL even though the test phase never exercised the patched artifact in its real import context. This crosses the interface to `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, which marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE or NEUTRAL. That can falsely close bugs through the NK bug-closed gate in later rounds, misleading both the insect brain summaries and reviewers with a verified-fix status that was never validated against the patched codebase.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — in `evaluate_fix()`, copy the full source tree needed for evaluation into the temp directory, write the patch at the same relative path inside that tree, and run `test_cmd` against that sandbox root so imports and path arguments resolve to the patched copy rather than the live repo.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when it introduces new issues, because it sums net deltas across different tools and only checks whether the total is positive. Example from the code: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; if a fix removes two ruff warnings (`-2`) but introduces one new pyright error (`+1`), `total_net == -1` and the verdict becomes SAFE. That is silently wrong because a new type or security issue is still a regression.
FOLLOW: Downstream, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` treats SAFE and NEUTRAL as programmatic verification and sets `finding.verified = True`. A compensating decrease in style/security/type counts can therefore hide a newly introduced correctness or security regression, causing the system to close a bug and deduplicate future reports against a bad fix. This directly degrades reviewer trust because the endocrine layer is the only mechanical gate claiming the fix is non-harmful.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — treat any per-tool positive delta (`net_type_errors > 0` or `net_ruff_errors > 0` or `net_bandit_issues > 0`) as HARMFUL before considering aggregate reductions; only return SAFE when no tool regresses and at least one metric improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` computes pre-fix baselines on the original file path and post-fix counts on a temp file whose directory/package context is different. Pyright, mypy, and even ruff/bandit can emit different diagnostics depending on import resolution and project config discovery. Because the comparison is original-path vs isolated-temp-file, the net deltas are not a like-for-like measurement of the patch effect. Evidence: pre counts use `target_path`; post counts use `patched_path` in a fresh temp directory containing only one file.
FOLLOW: This makes fix evaluation verdicts noisy and can be silently wrong in both directions: imports/config may disappear in temp isolation and create false HARMFULs, or project-level checks may be skipped and create false SAFEs. Those wrong verdicts feed directly into immune-stage verification, bug closure, and round-to-round suppression of duplicate findings.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute both baseline and post-fix diagnostics inside the same sandbox environment: copy the relevant project tree to temp, measure diagnostics on the unmodified sandbox file first, then patch that sandbox copy and re-measure there.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the health scan feature does not actually run all tools promised by the module contract. The file header and constants advertise `crosshair` and `mypy`, but `scan_health()` only invokes pyright, ruff, bandit, and mypy; there is no `run_crosshair()` and no CrossHair execution path anywhere in `endocrine.py`. This is distinct from the existing dead-constant report because the externally documented “Health scan — static analysis (pyright/ruff/bandit)” plus top-level tool list implies a working tool path that never fires.
FOLLOW: Downstream, any consumer trusting endocrine’s tool coverage will assume symbolic execution contributed to the health signal when it did not. That weakens defect detection for path-sensitive bugs and makes tool-availability accounting incomplete, because `tools_available` never reports crosshair at all despite the advertised capability.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove CrossHair from the documented/declared health-scan tool set for the PoC until an actual `run_crosshair()` integration exists.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0020 | The issue is not just unused declarations. The module-level contract and tool list advertise CrossHair as part of the endocrine toolchain, but `scan_health()` never includes it in execution or `tools_available`, so health-scan coverage is materially overstated to downstream consumers.

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()`’s target-file resolution is substring-based and can patch the wrong file when multiple source paths share names or partial paths. `_find_target_file()` returns the first `source_path` where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A mention like `endocrine.py` or a common fragment can match unrelated paths, especially in larger benches. This is an interface bug because fix evaluation is keyed by finding description text rather than canonical file metadata.
FOLLOW: If the wrong file is selected, endocrine can report a fix as applied and SAFE/HARMFUL for a completely different file from the finding’s real target. That contaminates verification results, causes misattributed `original_file`, and can mark unrelated findings verified in the immune pipeline.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to exact normalized suffix matches against extracted path candidates, preferring the longest exact suffix match, and do not fall back to substring containment.
VERIFIED: TRUE
